Debug mode writes per-packet TRACE lines to plugins/AuditTrail/debug/trace-N.log at ~1.4 MB/s; the trace files reached ~101 MB (disk 23 MB -> 127 MB of 443 MB) within ~30 s and would have filled the volume in a few minutes. args.actions: 1) Baseline status/logs/fs_du at shift start: healthy, 23 MB disk. 2) After 30 s wait, status showed disk 58 MB; fs_du located plugins/AuditTrail/debug/trace-0.log (44 MB) and latest.log showed "[AuditTrail] config reloaded (debug=true)" at 08:25:19. 3) Declared incident. 4) Read plugins/AuditTrail/config.yml (debug: true, retention-days: 30) and sampled the trace file (per-packet TRACE network logging, no user data). 5) Wrote plugins/AuditTrail/config.yml back to `debug: false` / `retention-days: 30`; plugin hot-reloaded at 08:25:45 ("config reloaded (debug=false)") - no restart needed. 6) Waited 10 s and confirmed disk flat at 127 MB and trace file mtimes frozen at 08:25:45 (writer stopped). 7) Deleted plugins/AuditTrail/debug (trace-0.log 51 MB + trace-1.log 50 MB, 101 MB total of regenerable debug output); disk returned to 23 MB. 8) Monitored for ~90 more seconds: disk stable at 23 MB, config unchanged, no debug dir recreated, no further AuditTrail reloads, TPS 20 throughout, both players stayed online.
args.residual_risk: The source of the 08:25:19 config change (debug: true) was not identified - it was not a console command and nothing in the server log attributes it. If the same actor/process flips the flag again, the trace logging will resume at ~1.4 MB/s and fill the 443 MB volume in a few minutes. Recommend finding who/what edited plugins/AuditTrail/config.yml (file permissions, deploy tooling, admin access), adding a disk-usage alert, and asking the AuditTrail maintainers for a size cap/rotation limit on debug traces. The plugin's audit.log and all world data were untouched.
